Research · Genealogy audit

Family tree completeness report

What changed in the genealogy, which records are visible, and where evidence is still needed.

Individual data review · November 11, 2026

All 510 current records have an individual review entry: 498 public FamilySearch profiles, eight owner-approved records, and four entries with unresolved identity or source evidence. Twenty-three public profiles list no attached historical documents. A completed comparison does not certify every historical claim.

Read the individual results and unresolved evidence

The previous homepage used four separate lookup rules. The maternal branches exposed a short direct line and left out documented relatives and links. Downard and Lambson also showed some records as non-interactive cards. The tree now uses the same people and relationship records as the directory.

Each person counts once, under their primary archive branch. The current display count means a selectable roster card; direct-line cards are still only shortcuts. Disconnected means no path through recorded relationships to that branch’s starting person. A blank spouse or parent field means the archive has no recorded link, including when no marriage is known. Matching names are candidates for review, never grounds to merge records. One Peterson record is shown anonymously.
